item.author: Malte Landwehr (Peec AI)
item.title: How ChatGPT Shopping Picks Products: US vs Europe (BrightonSEO 2026)
item.note: Hand-read by Claude on 2026-10-22 at Kelian's request. Analysis: mvp/content-agent/RESEARCH-PEEC-CHATGPT-SHOPPING-2026-10-22.md

claims.claim: ChatGPT debug logs show US shopping now retrieves products from OpenAI's own index (Labrador), filled by feeds merchants send to OpenAI or through Shopify, while in Europe it still scrapes Google Shopping through SerpAPI.
claims.sample_size: debug logs of individual sessions, count not given

claims.claim: In US ChatGPT Shopping debug logs, every candidate product's description is cut at exactly 50 tokens (about 40 words or 250 characters) at the product-scoring stage; nothing after that is scored there.
claims.sample_size: debug logs of individual sessions, count not given

claims.claim: For one US running-shoes query, 41 candidate products were retrieved, 32 went into the prompt block and 5 were shown; candidates carry host, title, GTIN and verified status and are scored with embeddings, BM25 keyword matching, ANN and RRF.

US ChatGPT Shopping drops candidates without a 'verified seller' attribute entirely, and in one query a low-trust shop with 25 candidate products had none shown; where the attribute comes from is not known.
claims.sample_size: debug logs of individual sessions, count not given

claims.claim: US ChatGPT Shopping de-duplicates the same product in different sizes; Peec advises sending every variant as its own feed item so a brand can take more of the shown slots (advice, not measured).
Links from the feed-based US ChatGPT Shopping experience end in utm_medium=feed, so those clicks can be attributed even though the app sends no normal referrer.
claims.sample_size: debug logs of individual sessions, count not given

claims.claim: In Europe, ChatGPT pools Google Shopping results from about five fan-out queries round-robin (113 products in one example), keeps 18, and uses no embeddings, BM25, GTIN or verified-seller check; it takes about 4 seconds against 0.6 for the US index.
The US ChatGPT shopping subsystem receives the user's current and home location, inferred gender with a confidence score, and the merchants and marketplaces already shown to or clicked by that user.
claims.sample_size: debug logs of individual sessions, count not given

claims.claim: For the text around the product carousel, ChatGPT searches separate indexes for web, Reddit, news (past 7 days and general), PDFs, YouTube and Wikipedia; in one example 42 candidate sources were retrieved and 1 was cited.
US ChatGPT debug logs list an A/B test called 'No Amazon' that shows shopping results with zero Amazon listings.
claims.sample_size: debug logs of individual sessions, count not given

claims.claim: In UK ChatGPT chats that show a product gallery, listicles and category pages are cited as sources more often than in chats without one.

In UK e-commerce chats, shops are the most common source domains while aggregators and marketplaces are rarely sources and, when they are, the least likely to get an inline citation; non-commercial sites such as reviews and manufacturers are the most likely to get one.
claims.related_like: %64.7% of citations for non-branded U.S. shopping questions%

claims.claim: Since GPT-5.6, listicles' share of ChatGPT sources has fallen (still the largest type), Reddit-driven discussion pages have fallen sharply, and product pages have risen.
UK ChatGPT product galleries usually show 4 products (1 to 7, rarely more), and Amazon is the top merchant in almost every category; Decathlon leads only in outdoor.
When a product gallery appears, ChatGPT adds a brand name to its fan-out searches far more often than a merchant name; merchants are added mainly for 'where can I buy this' questions.

In US tests across several AI engines, short generic shopping prompts drew more retailer sources and listicles, while detailed prompts drew fewer retailers and more non-commercial advice and comparison articles; site: searches appeared in 7-12% of fan-outs for detailed prompts and almost never for short ones.

In Peec AI's e-commerce data with Ahrefs Domain Rating, domains below DR 20 were rarely cited; above that, the citation rate per URL was similar, and high-DR domains won mainly by having more URLs in the sources.
claims.measured_by: Peec AI with Ahrefs DR data
